facts.detail: A signed-up provider pays £10.34 per calendar day when total loss of service is not fully repaired after two full working days.
A missed engineer appointment or cancellation with less than 24 hours notice attracts £32.31.
Delayed activation attracts £6.46 for each calendar day including the missed start date.
The voluntary scheme covers residential fixed broadband and landline products of participating providers.

guard_streams.write_limit: Compensation entitlement does not measure parcel speed, technology or coverage.

facts.detail: Delayed starts and missed appointments are compensated automatically without a customer claim.
For loss of service the customer must report the fault before the repair clock applies.
Compensation is normally credited no later than 30 calendar days after resolution, cancellation or the missed appointment.
Home equipment, contractual breach, customer-caused failure or prevention of repair can exclude payment.

guard_streams.write_limit: Billing credits and scheme exclusions are customer-account evidence only.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom broadband and landline faults guide

facts.detail: Customers receiving speeds far below the original estimate may have protection under the voluntary speeds code.
Unresolved faults should first follow the provider's formal complaints procedure.
A complaint still unresolved after six weeks can be referred to an independent ADR scheme.
A deadlock letter can permit referral before the six-week point.

guard_streams.write_limit: Complaint and ADR status cannot populate parcel network fields.

facts.detail: Number spoofing changes caller ID information presented to the recipient.
Scammers may hide their identity or imitate the number of a genuine person or organisation.
Some caller-ID modification can have legitimate uses such as presenting a callback number.
A displayed number alone is not reliable proof of the caller's true origin.

guard_streams.write_limit: Caller-ID behaviour is unrelated to parcel broadband availability.

facts.detail: The release contains UPRN-level OMR determinations, current connectivity, future commercial plans and BDUK intervention plans.
It does not comprehensively identify historical BDUK delivery through vouchers, Gigahubs or Superfast programmes.
BDUK identified supplier-name errors in the original publication.
Corrected files and a no-region CSV were published on 2 February 2026.

guard_streams.write_limit: Corrected planning data still cannot replace accepted Ofcom r2 postcode evidence.

facts.detail: BDUK publishes monthly contract-level updates for contracted and built premises.
The collection lists monthly releases from October 2025 through July 2026.
The collection was updated on 20 July 2026 to add the July release.
The collection relates to Project Gigabit support for hard-to-reach communities.

guard_streams.write_limit: Collection cadence and programme purpose do not identify exact delivered parcels.

facts.detail: The table is a snapshot of BDUK data held on 21 October 2025.
Figures are rounded to the nearest ten and totals may not sum.
Contracted figures include initial scope and can exclude deferred premises.
Variable ingestion lag means the table should not assess contractual milestones.

guard_streams.write_limit: Rounded lagged management data cannot prove current parcel readiness.

facts.detail: The November table is a snapshot of data held on 17 November 2025.
Deferred-scope premises may not appear in contracted totals.
Management figures measure a different concept from BDUK official statistics.
Delivery can precede ingestion into BDUK systems by a variable interval.

guard_streams.write_limit: A monthly contract snapshot cannot determine exact parcel coverage.

facts.detail: The December table is a snapshot of data held on 17 December 2025.
The Fibrus Northern Ireland contract was excluded because of ingestion lag.
Values are rounded and contracted totals cover initial scope only.
Built contracted premises are not directly comparable with subsidy-delivery official statistics.

guard_streams.write_limit: Omissions and differing concepts require fail-closed parcel interpretation.

facts.detail: The collection summarises local and regional Project Gigabit contracts awarded to suppliers.
The collection was last updated on 17 December 2025 when Northern Ireland was added.
It links awarded local, regional and Openreach framework contracts.
Presence in the collection records procurement, not current address-level orderability.

guard_streams.write_limit: A contract index cannot establish current parcel service.

facts.detail: Wessex Internet is the supplier for the New Forest contract.
The contract value is nearly £14 million.
The award targets around 10,500 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed in March 2023 and detailed planning and network build precede service.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional award scope is not exact current parcel coverage.

facts.detail: Fibrus is the supplier for the Cumbria contract.
The contract value is £108.5 million.
The award covers up to 59,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed on 1 December 2022 and premise scope remains subject to planning and technical change.

guard_streams.write_limit: Awarded scope and anticipated dates do not prove present parcel serviceability.

facts.detail: Borderlink, the parent company of GoFibre, received the contract.

The award targets more than 3,750 premises.
The contract was signed on 14 October 2022 and construction precedes service requests.

guard_streams.write_limit: Procurement and planned build do not establish live parcel availability.

facts.detail: Borderlink, the parent company of GoFibre, received the Teesdale contract.
